evidence.code: // Ctrl+Shift+R is browser hard refresh — only hijack when columns are selected
showMessage("Select at least one span of 2+ columns to realign.", 3000);

verdicts.detail: Most details match: Ctrl+Shift+R (e.shiftKey) calls realignSelectedBlock(); isolated single columns are skipped because columnRuns filters to runs of 2+ columns (realign-region.js:128); and realignSelectedBlock requires at least one span of 2+ columns (script.js:15447-15448). The mismatch is 'otherwise the browser's hard-refresh applies': the handleKeyDown guard that decides preventDefault/hard-refresh is `state.selectedColumns.size >= 2` — a TOTAL selected-column count (script.js:9652), not a contiguous-span check. When two or more NON-adjacent isolated single columns are selected (no span of 2+ columns), the guard still passes, e.preventDefault() fires (so NO browser hard-refresh), and realignSelectedBlock instead shows the toast 'Select at least one span of 2+ columns to realign.' and returns. The browser hard-refresh actually applies only when fewer than 2 total columns are selected, so the stated hard-refresh behaviour does not match the code in the isolated-single-columns case the claim describes.

note: Claim 13k verdicted MISMATCH. The Ctrl+Shift+R shortcut, the "isolated single columns are skipped" behavior (columnRuns filter for runs of 2+), and the "need at least one span of 2+ columns" requirement (realignSelectedBlock toast) all match. However, the claim ties 'otherwise the browser's hard-refresh applies' to 'need at least one span of 2+ columns', but the handleKeyDown guard deciding preventDefault is `state.selectedColumns.size >= 2` (total count, script.js:9652), not a span check. With 2+ non-adjacent isolated single columns selected, preventDefault fires (no hard-refresh) and a toast is shown instead; the browser hard-refresh applies only when <2 total columns are selected.
